realDataReads: FORBIDDEN: every return is synthetic; geometry constants are copied from committed outcome-blind readiness reports
purpose: Prerequisite P3 of us-cash-profitability-signal-v1: does an interval for the H63 controlled factor spread keep its nominal error rates under the study's geometry? Not an alpha study; a PASS says nothing about whether the feature predicts returns.

inferentialTarget.statistic: S_t = sum_i w(t,i) Y(t,i); w = gross-2 weights proportional to the OLS residual of the feature's within-date percentile rank on sector dummies and the percentile ranks of four controls; Y = 63-session forward return (synthetic, additive)
inferentialTarget.estimand: theta = E[S_t] over weekly signal dates
inferentialTarget.unit: fraction of capital per 63 sessions earned by $1 long / $1 short (x4 = annualised); a RETURN, not a correlation
inferentialTarget.interval: one interval reported as two one-sided 95% bounds (two-sided 90%)
inferentialTarget.decisionRule: lower bound > 0 -> SUPPORTED; upper bound <= 0 -> REFUTED; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE (the two cannot both hold)

source.controlCorrelations: docs/us-readiness/us-multifactor-pit-readiness-v1.json featureRedundancy (mom121~vol252 -0.116; roe/operatingMargin~vol252 -0.098/-0.238 averaged -0.17; mom121~roe/operatingMargin ~0.10); entries marked ASSUMED have no committed measurement

geometry.persistenceRationale: accounting variables: quarterly autocorrelation 0.85 (0.85^(1/13) weekly) and observed only at a staggered quarterly filing week; momentum: 51 of 52 weeks of the 12-month window overlap; volatility and traded value: slow-moving. ASSUMED values, not measured from returns

baseReturns.note: daily units; control premia are nonzero so the null 'no incremental information' is tested while the controls themselves earn premia; market and sector shocks are common; idiosyncratic volatility is cross-sectionally heteroskedastic and follows a common stochastic-volatility regime

dgps.name: NONLINEAR_EXPOSURE_STRESS
dgps.why: returns load on latent characteristic values while the weights neutralise RANKS: tests whether control premia leak into the 'incremental' spread. A construct check, not an inference check; reported against zero, never gating

methods.CT_SN: calendar-time attribution (each realised daily contribution assigned to its calendar week) + Lobato/Shao self-normalised interval, alpha_inference_calibration_v4.calendar_time_sn_interval
methods.SD_SN: self-normalised interval on the overlapping signal-date series (v3), comparator
methods.SD_NW_L12: Newey-West Bartlett, 12 lags (the H63 overlap in weeks), normal critical value, signal-date series, comparator
methods.CT_NW_AUTO: Newey-West Bartlett on the calendar-time residual series, lags floor(4 (n/100)^(2/9)), normal critical value, comparator
methods.CT_CBB13: circular block bootstrap of calendar weeks, block 13 weeks, 499 draws, ratio estimator, percentile bounds, comparator
methods.snCriticalValueSource: Lobato (2001) U1 90% upper critical value (two-sided 90% = one-sided 95% per side); the repository's v3-v5 used the same table's 97.5% value 66.57. Checked by simulation in tests

acceptance.rationale: nominal one-sided error 0.05 per side and two-sided coverage 0.90; up to 1.5x the nominal error is tolerated, stricter than v4/v5 (which tolerated 2x miscoverage at 97.5%). Fixed before any replicate
acceptance.gating: the primary candidate on gating DGPs only; comparators are classified by the same rule and reported, never gating
acceptance.p3Rule: P3 PASS iff CT_SN is PASS in every gating DGP at 260 and 700 weeks. The 130-week cells decide only whether an interval may be quoted at the futility look; the futility rule itself uses no interval. Any FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE at 260 or 700 -> P3 BLOCKED (an INCONCLUSIVE is not resolved by rerunning; a new version would be a new protocol)
acceptance.estimandUnderNull: coverage is judged against theta = 0. Rank-linear exposures make the gross-2 residual weights exactly neutral to every sector and control premium ON THE SIGNAL DATE; within the 63-session window exposures drift weekly, so any remaining null mean is second order. It is not assumed away: the mean of the estimate across null replicates and its Monte Carlo interval are reported, and any such bias counts against coverage (conservative)

monteCarloDecision.failSideDecisionCountDefinition: 5 gating DGPs x 3 sample lengths x 4 metrics (coverage, lower-bound error, upper-bound error, undefined frequency) for the primary candidate

power.construction: a synthetic drift is added so a cohort's spread gains effect/252 per session (effect x 63/252 per H63); EXPLICITLY SYNTHETIC effect sizes, not estimates of any real effect
power.futility: non-binding look at the first 130 signal dates of each 260-week replicate: stop if the interim point estimate <= 0. Reported: P(stop) under the null and under each effect, and the power lost to stopping

prohibitions: no real return, price, label, model prediction or strategy PnL is read
no historical exploratory study is executed
no prospective study is registered or authorised
thresholds, DGPs, sample lengths, seed and replicate counts may not change after the first replicate; a change is a new contract version
